title: When Higher-Order Neyman Orthogonality Matches the Jets of a Causal Target
banked_reason: The sound locality counterexample and conditional bridge reached only letter tier; the field-level projection frontier is covered by Robins et al. 2017 plus standard approximation-width theory.
gap_reasons: The older load-bearing antecedents, especially Pfanzagl and Small--McLeish, have not been theorem-by-theorem compared to the bridge's two-law, off-truth, and lifting quantifiers, so absence of a published equivalent remains unsupported.

The bridge and reparameterization diagnostic are useful analytic audits, but the stated scope establishes no new estimator, rate, inference guarantee, or changed causal-MAR capability beyond known higher-order projection remedies, supporting letter rather than the required field tier.
proof_attempt_summary: The run developed a sound bounded counterexample to pointwise higher-order equivalence and a conditional locality bridge, but it stopped before formal derivation because the package remained at letter/subfield tier. The proposed MAR projection frontier collapsed against existing projected-HOIF theory and standard approximation-width arguments. A successor must retain the counterexample and compatibility distinction while adding a verified general equivalence and a genuinely new feasible inference result for an unknown ill-posed operator.
tldr: The project asks when kth-order Neyman flatness of a specified, possibly multi-observation estimating equation really forces its frozen-nuisance implicit root to have the same kth law-chart jet as the causal target. The candidate answer is an exact locality bridge: correct specification, exact \(C^k\) regularity, an invertible target Jacobian, lower-order flatness along the whole nearby diagonal, and target-preserving nuisance lifts yield an iff coordinate-jet result. A fully instantiated bounded Bernoulli family proves that pointwise matching cannot replace neighboring flatness. A separate Hilbert--Schmidt theorem prevents chart-jet equality from being mistaken for a finite-variance HOIF kernel, and a MAR mean consequence shows that the AIPW score's nonzero mixed second-order curvature survives every smooth locally invertible nuisance reparameterization, so genuine higher-order score design must change the moment rather than relabel its nuisance.
gap: Classical higher-order score, E-ancillary projection, information-equality, and implicit-functional theories already provide much of the surrounding calculus. What remains unresolved is a matched-quantifier criterion for one user-specified two-law-coordinate moment: exactly which off-truth lower-flatness and lifting conditions make its kth nuisance derivative equivalent to target-versus-frozen-root law-chart jet agreement, and which parts of that analytic tensor are finite-variance representable.
fill: Prove the exact implicit-root and diagonal-jet bridge with explicit regularity and lifting; prove the all-order Bernoulli separation in the same framework; give the self-contained second-order Hilbert--Schmidt range theorem; and establish the MAR coordinate-invariance obstruction. The project will stop or pivot if older theorem text matches the same two-law locality quantifiers or if the MAR consequence is already stated in this coordinate-invariant form.
